title: Vernier scale
summary: Vernier's 1631 subsidiary scale used coincident graduations to read fractions of a main scale division on angular or linear instruments.

title: Board of Longitude
summary: Established by the Longitude Act, the British commission administered rewards and support for practical methods and instruments for finding longitude at sea.

title: Ramsden screw-cutting lathe
summary: Ramsden's lathe combined a leadscrew, slide rest, and change gears to cut accurate threads used in further lathes and instrument-dividing machinery.

parents.reason: Rotating workholding and cutting geometry formed the lathe on which Ramsden added controlled screw-cutting feeds.
parents.directContribution: The lathe directly holds and rotates the workpiece during thread cutting; the leadscrew independently controls the cutting tool's axial advance.

parents.reason: A leadscrew coordinated the cutting tool's advance with workpiece rotation to generate a repeatable thread pitch.

title: Ramsden dividing engine
summary: Documented in Ramsden's 1777 publication, a precision screw-indexed machine engraved regular angular graduations on measuring instruments.

parents.reason: Ramsden's accurate screw-cutting lathes produced the precision screws used to index his dividing machinery.
The Board funded the engine on conditions requiring published construction details, access for other makers, and instruction in making copies.

title: Hounslow Heath survey baseline
summary: Roy's team measured a five-mile survey base with calibrated glass rods and thermal corrections, establishing a known length for the Anglo-French triangulation.

parents.reason: Solid glass supplied the calibrated measuring rods used repeatedly along the baseline; their lengths resisted humidity changes during measurement.

title: Ramsden great theodolite
summary: Delivered in 1787, Ramsden's large survey instrument combined accurately divided angular scales with microscope and screw readouts for very fine angle measurement.

parents.reason: One of Ramsden's dividing engines engraved the instrument's horizontal circle at regular fifteen-arcminute intervals.
Microscopes with adjustable cross wires read positions between the instrument's engraved angular graduations.
The sighting telescope aimed at distant survey stations while the horizontal and vertical scales recorded its orientation.

title: Anglo-French triangulation results
summary: Completed calculations linked the Greenwich and Paris observatories through measured bases and survey triangles, demonstrating a precise geodetic survey across the Channel.

parents.reason: The measured Hounslow baseline supplied a known length from which the survey's connected triangles could be calculated.
Ramsden's instrument measured the survey triangle angles during the 1787–1788 observations used in the final calculations.
Triangulation combined measured bases with observed angles to compute the relative positions of the observatories.
